newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds firm, yield curve steepens again.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds firm, yield curve steepens again.

text.p: *Australian bond yields closed sharply lower with demand generally centring on the short end, causing the yield curve to continue its steepening since last Friday's official rate cut.
*U.S. debt firm in Tokyo after Monday's U.S. holiday.
Australian bonds finally shook off the solid profit-taking seen in the aftermath of Friday's official interest rate cut as investors saw value at the short-end of the curve.

Traders said the three-year bond's 100 basis point yield gap at the start of the day over the official cash rate, now at 5.5 percent, was seen as too much of a lure given policy is expected to be on hold for some time.
"It's a pretty safe part of the curve to get into," added one trader at a European bank in Sydney.
Domestic institutions led the way in initially, followed by Asian buyers later in the day, traders said.
Such demand saw the yield curve continue its steepening trend since the rate cut with the three/10-year futures spread having now put on some 18 basis points since Thursday's close.
Demand for short-dated stock also filtered through to the long-end, and also found support from a firm tone in U.S. Treasuries in Tokyo trading after Monday's U.S. holiday.
A 6.5 percent jump in local first quarter capital expenditure failed to make an impression, being offset by a downward revision in forward investment estimates.

The second estimate for business investment intentions for 1997/98 included in the data was A$36.57 billion, up from a substantially revised-down A$31.90 billion first estimate and an original A$34.68 billion.
Peter Munckton, senior economist at Bankers Trust Australia, said the new survey was disappointing for the investment outlook and supported the RBA's recent rate cut.
"Indeed, on the RBA's measure, the investment outlook for 1997/98 has fallen from 6.0 percent to close to 1.0 percent," Munckton added.

The firm tone saw spreads to the dollar bloc narrow, and the three-year differential to the U.S. close in on parity again, having briefly tested it in immediate reaction on the rate cut last Friday. U.S. April consumer confidence and existing home sales are due later on Tuesday.

The 10-year bond contract came close to testing at 92.480 after overcoming 92.410 in early trading, while the three-year contract ended at 93.57 resistance after breaching 93.50/93.52 barrier just after the opening.
